subject: F1 25 AI modding via Swofty Launcher, for the Verve driver-personality port

confidence_scale.proven: stated as proven in the Swofty catalogue, or read directly from source code
confidence_scale.decoded: from a decompiled function with an RE note describing the data flow (Swofty L1/L2)
confidence_scale.inferred: from key names, value shapes or docs wording; no code read
confidence_scale.hypothesis: our interpretation; needs the listed test

findings.claim: F1 25 has six per-driver AI characteristics (aggression, control, mistakes, reaction_speed, speed_in, speed_out), each 0..1, derived from the racecraft/awareness/pace ratings through 'distribution' curves on six DriverCharacteristicOverride rows.
evidence: tools/gamedb/catalog/keys.tsv.gz: driver_statistics.driver_statistics.driver_characteristic_overrides.DriverCharacteristicOverride_N.{driver_statistic (racecraft|awareness|pace), driver_characteristic (enum of six), distribution (curve minx 0 maxx 1 miny 0 maxy 1)}
re/db/functions.tsv Ai_Parse_DriverParameterMap 0x14065aec0: 'bilinear map of difficulty x driver characteristic (aggression, control, mistakes, reaction_speed, speed_in, speed_out)'
re/db/subsystems/ai.md inbox 2026-10-29: live record effective +0xa8 aggression, +0xac control, +0xb0 mistakes, +0xb4 reaction_speed, +0xb8 speed_in, +0xbc speed_out
findings.implications: Verve scalars map onto an existing 0..1 model; no new systems needed for v0.1.

findings.claim: Each driver row carries driver_characteristics.{aggression,control,mistakes,reaction_speed,speed_in,speed_out} fields. Whether the AI uses these row values or the rating-derived values (driver_characteristic_overrides curves) is UNKNOWN (Q-17).
findings.confidence: proven (fields exist, values dumped); unknown (precedence vs the rating curves)
evidence: addons/classicseasons/classic-seasons-2024/db/season.json fields list for entrants.drivers.driver includes all six plus preferred_tracks
findings.implications: v0.1 writes these row fields. If the rating curves take precedence for drivers with a statistics holder (every 2025 grid driver has one), v0.1's row writes are no-ops there. Issue #7 decides.
findings.correction: 2026-10-30 stock dump: stock DOES set them (the original claim 'stock sets none' and 'a non-negative value overrides the derived characteristic' are withdrawn). Every dumped driver row carries hand-tuned non-negative values (Verstappen aggression 1, control 0.96, mistakes 0.75, reaction 0.85, speed_in 1, speed_out 0.99; Bearman 0.65/0.765/0.65/0.65/0.68/0.78; Alonso 0.93/0.97/0.90/1.0/0.93/0.94). The RE note's 'raw +0xf0 / overrides +0x108 (negative = none)' fits either reading: row = raw base with the rating curves as the overrides, or the reverse. See F-28, Q-17.

findings.claim: Eleven per-package parameter maps turn (difficulty, characteristic) into controller factors; six of them still separate drivers at high difficulty; brake_off_time, slide_confidence, alongside_awareness and wet_weather_ability are 1 (or 0) at every corner in stock, i.e. dead.
evidence: docs/reference/gamedb/schema.md rows ai_vehicle_package_config.driver_parameter_maps.* (43/43 rows): braking_distance_factor hi/lo 1.15..1.25 vs hi/hi 1; corner_curvature_factor 0.92 vs 1; follow_speed_factor 1.05 vs 1; alongside_space_factor 1.15 vs 1; throttle_exit_fallibility 1 vs 0.75; wet_weather_ability 1,1,1,1
findings.implications: Personality survives the 110 slider. Wet complaint plausibly linked to the dead wet map; consumer not found.

findings.claim: 84 per-driver ai_driver_config.* keys (alongside 8, blocking 16, cede_position 6, divebomb_defense 4, exit_fallibility 2, offset_variation 7, overtake 19, race_start 9, space_seeking 13) exist on every driver row and are identical on all 197 stock drivers.
evidence: addons/classicseasons/classic-seasons-2024/db/season.json fields block (the 84 names; 'every listed field must exist on the source row')
re/db/subsystems/ai.md inbox 2026-10-29: 'ai_driver_config parsed per driver (0x142463b40 -> 0x14065dc50 at 0x14246671e; default_driver copy 0x14249a4f0) but stock identical for all 197 drivers'
docs/stock/ai_driver_config.csv: all 84 keys identical for default_driver, max_verstappen, oliver_bearman, fernando_alonso
findings.implications: This is the 'same decision every time' complaint and the v0.2 surface. Catalogued in docs/ai_driver_config_keys.csv.

findings.claim: Per-driver corner-exit throttle error is computed once per exit from a random draw mapped through the driver's exit_fallibility.throttle_error_practice (sessions 1-4) or throttle_error_qualifying_race (sessions 5-18) curve, scaled, capped by the per-car ai_vehicle_config.exit_fallibility caps, and suppressed while yaw exceeds max_yaw_angle_deg.
evidence: re/db/functions.tsv Ai_Read_GeneralSettings_3 0x1405f5dd0 notes (per-car AI data +0x348 / +0x350; caps at +0x300/+0x308/+0x310; max_yaw +0x318)
findings.implications: Strongest decoded per-driver Consistency lever; A-rated in the catalogue.

findings.claim: AI race-start reaction time is drawn from U[0.28 - 0.24kr, 0.42 - 0.18kr] with r = reaction_speed and k a per-session factor; the bounds come from ai_driver_config.race_start.{min,max}_reaction_time_{lower,upper}_bound; bad starts come from the mistakes characteristic via the bad_start bounds. Logged on channel RaceStarts.
evidence: re/db/subsystems/ai.md inbox 2026-10-29: 'Race start 0x1406527c0 (ptr 0x145637220): reaction U[0.28-0.24kr, 0.42-0.18kr] (k = R+0x14c, r = +0xb4), bad start from mistakes +0xb0'
re/db/functions.tsv Ai_Parse_RaceStartConfig 0x14065e040; Ai_RaceStart_ReactionTime 0x1406527c0 log 'Reaction Time for driver with vehicle id %d: %f'
findings.implications: Directly measurable readout for reaction_speed and the race_start bounds; use it as the first verification.
findings.correction: Stock bounds from the dump: min_reaction_time lower/upper 0.04/0.28, max_reaction_time 0.24/0.42, min_bad_start 0.04/0.06, max_bad_start 0.28/0.42. The handoff's 'min = [0.28, 0.42], max = [0.04, 0.24]' had the labels swapped.
findings.runtime_note: B-0003 (#33, 5 stock benchmark starts at Austria): the stock field (vehicle 19 excluded) never started under 0.171 s; per-start mean 0.248-0.265 s, SD 0.036-0.058. That fits the formula only with k ~0.5 (r ~0.85 -> U[0.18, 0.34], mean ~0.26); at k = 1 it would be U[0.08, 0.27]. Vehicle 19 (a Ferrari, possibly the player car) fits k*r ~1 (0.054-0.109 s in 5 of 7 starts). The per-start drift (~0.017 s) suggests k varies by session. Fit by the supervisor review on #36.

findings.claim: The overtake decision evaluates ai_driver_config.overtake.overlap_percentage (curve) at x = the driver's effective aggression, only when the attacker is within 0.5 lap.
evidence: re/db/subsystems/ai.md inbox 2026-10-29: 'Overtake helper 0x140650150 evaluates ai_driver_config overtake.overlap_percentage (config +0x1d0, curve **(aiobj+0x408)) at x = aggression (only if attacker within 0.5 lap)'
findings.implications: aggression is live in overtaking; the curve itself need not vary per driver.

findings.claim: AI ERS push reasons are gated by per-car battery levels: build gap 0.7, close gap 0.6, in/out lap 0.47, overtake 0.25 (0.15 xmode_passive, 0.30 xmode_enabled), defend 1.0; target battery 0.9 - 0.4 x lap progress (0.9 - 0.15 x in overtake mode); mode from the per-track ERS table.
evidence: re/db/functions.tsv Ai_Ers_DecidePushReasons 0x1406487a0 notes; re/db/subsystems/ai.md inbox (ERSBoost behaviour test, vtable 0x145636d40 slot 4)
findings.implications: The 'AI never defends / infinite ERS' complaints have per-car and per-track data levers.

findings.claim: The 0-110 difficulty slider is calibrated per track per vehicle package by 10-point tables tracks.Track_N.ai_track_difficulties.<package>.{time, difficulty_ratio, mass_ratio} plus max_dificulty_no_balast_slider_position = 100; difficulty_ratio reaches 1.0 at point 7 and mass_ratio drops below 1 (to ~0.92-0.94) only at points 8-10.
findings.confidence: proven (keys read by exe) + hypothesis (index meaning)
evidence: tools/gamedb/meanings.tsv: 'ai_track_difficulties.*: proven, time and max_dificulty_no_balast_slider_position are read by the exe'

tools/gamedb/catalog/keys.tsv.gz examples for f1_2025_vehicle_package: time 87.83,85.66,83.56,81.37,79.21,78.10,...; difficulty_ratio 0.41,0.455,0.575,0.655,0.805,0.895,1,1,1,1; mass_ratio 1x7,0.980,0.960,0.938
re/db/subsystems/ai.md: 'AI difficulty slider (0-110) application NOT located statically' (the code side); re/db/subsystems/car.md#ai: no difficulty-keyed grip/power/drag multiplier exists
findings.implications: Difficulty ceiling and per-track pace swings are data-editable. Above 100 the AI advantage is mass, which predicts straight-line and traction gains, matching the top community complaints.

findings.claim: Race-form variation is global: 84 ai.driver_variation.in_race curves are picked per session type with availability flags; addedLapTime = (1 - curve(progress)) * lap_time_variations (default 4 s); no per-driver weighting exists.
findings.implications: Per-driver Consistency-as-form needs a native hook (v0.3).

findings.claim: A database 'set' op resolves the key by FNV hash under the selected row and keeps the stock type tag; it does not need the key to be in the launcher's catalogue. The catalogue matters for add-row completeness.
evidence: packages/core/src/activation/dbx.rs set_text(): get(key) -> tag, else Error::Resolve('no such key'); put(key, tag, value)
findings.implications: ai_driver_config.* keys are settable per driver without a fields block.

findings.claim: Whether Grand Prix mode reads the driver statistics component (ratings) is unknown; career freezes ratings per season; driver.ratings.read hook exists for career.
evidence: docs/std/systems/drivers.md: 'Grand Prix and Time Trial use base ratings in every box. Whether Grand Prix reads the statistics component at all needs reverse engineering.'
findings.implications: If GP mode ignores ratings, driver-row overrides may be the only route to personality in GP races.

findings.claim: The Swofty 1.6 registry/event API for AI (ai::vehicle_configs, package_maps, track_packs, general, difficulty, ai.config.load, ai.settings.resolve) is design-only; 1.6.0 ships only the ai.controller.update payload, itself unverified (T145).
findings.implications: Write 1.5-style database ops; do not build on the C++ registry examples for AI yet.

findings.claim: The game's internal log channels RaceStarts, CANNED_EVENTS, AI_VARIATION, QUALI_PACE_DEBUG, GARAGECREW, GARAGE can be copied into swofty/loader.log via swofty/session.json game_log.channels (or SWOFTY_GAME_LOG_CHANNELS).
findings.implications: Cheap verification without a native plugin.

findings.claim: Per-driver strategy tendencies already vary in stock (driver_strategy.*, 10 keys, ranges e.g. fastest_strategy_base_selection_chance 0.15..0.85).
findings.implications: v0.1 re-derives three of them from Risk; this replaces editorial values, it does not add a mechanism.

findings.claim: The pit crew garage push-in is a GarageCrewInstanceLogic state machine (StateWaitPushIntoGarage -> StateZoomIntoMonitor -> StateCarIsReadyForTrack -> StateSendCarToTrack_P3) driven by Game_GarageCrew_StateTransition, separate from CutsceneManager cutscenes (podium, grid, garage, results, terminal_damage, intro_flag), whose scripts expose requestShutdown / testAndClrRequestStop / setStateShutdown.
evidence: re/db/subsystems/session.md 2026-10-25 vmknolle: pit status chain garage 0/9 -> 10 -> 11/12 -> 13 -> 14 -> 1
findings.implications: Skip-all-cutscenes is a native plugin; the garage skip needs a traced state chain and is option-gated.

findings.claim: Parser functions Ai_Parse_{Overtake,Blocking,SpaceSeeking,CedePosition}Config are annotated 'from ai_vehicle_config' in functions.tsv, but their leaf names match the per-driver ai_driver_config groups, and a later note places the per-driver parse at 0x142463b40 -> 0x14065dc50. Attribution unresolved.
evidence: re/db/subsystems/ai.md#vocabulary: per-car blocking has 5 differently named keys, overtake 4, exit_fallibility 4
findings.implications: Does not block setting the per-driver keys (they exist on the rows); blocks interpreting the parser notes as per-driver semantics.

findings.claim: Simulated and skipped sessions use baked lap times, driver statistics and randomness, not physics or R&D.
evidence: docs/std/systems/ai.md limits: 'Simulated sessions: They use baked lap times, driver statistics, and randomness, not physics or R&D.'
findings.implications: The pace rating must track Verve Pace or skipped sessions contradict driven ones; v0.1 writes it.

findings.claim: Existing third-party AI addons on Swofty as of 2026-10-30: Kizikafuka 'Collision & AI Tweaks' (kizi.ai-tweaks; per-car buffer, throttle cut, lost-control angle, steering PID, TC off, native contact handling), 'More Aggressive AI Track Pack' (track markup: removes limited-overtake zones, widens racing limits), vmknolle sc-unlapping and red-flag-pit (native, use Ai_Apply_TetherSpeedCap and site_Ai_ScFollowFlagCmp). None varies behaviour per driver.
evidence: docs/design/std-2/coverage.md 'AI Racing Tweaks'; re/db/subsystems/ai.md inbox 2026-10-29 (vmknolle exports)
findings.implications: Per-driver personality is an open niche.

findings.claim: Addon options surface in five places: the launcher Addons row (grouped by `category`), the per-addon ADDON SETTINGS page in game, a `career_setup` page between a career tile and the wizard (launcher >= 1.5.13), a Team HQ `hub_tab` per data group, and a race-MFD `hud.mfd` page. `binds: db` values are baked at build (rebuild + restart), `binds: native` values are live. `career_setup` values are profile-level; a plugin copies them into career storage at creation.
findings.implications: A per-profile My Team preset is pure data; a true wizard step is native. No cross-addon 'Verve category' exists in game.

findings.claim: The `career_setup` route is documented as a copy of the Driver Career route (`career_wizard_driver_career_to_f1`) with `next` a screen in `flow_career_season_setup.erp`; attaching it to the My Team tile is undocumented.
findings.implications: Option C of HANDOFF §11.4 needs Q-13 answered first.

findings.claim: Players' My Team complaints (EA forums, Oct 2025 to Oct 2026): cost cap never binds; thousands of unusable R&D points; all upgrades bought in season 1; AI teams maxed in 2-3 seasons; a maxed AI car ~1 s/lap faster than a maxed player car; regulation changes touch parts not departments.
findings.implications: 'Harder' = tighter player economy and slower progression, plus a fairness fix for the ceiling; not faster AI.

findings.claim: The My Team economy is data: starting cash per background outcome (0 / 2.5M / 7.5M), team cash rate modifiers (player 0.7/1.25, AI 0.6/1.25), 80 one-shot cash rewards (100k-500k), sponsor income per decal tier (5k-25k), budget pools with caps (1.5M-100M) and enforce flags, cost-cap cutoffs (0.95/0.9) and breach game values, per-team initial RP (1000-1750) incl. AI teams, practice-programme RP multipliers, R&D cost/time/fail scales as MyTeam attribute defaults (280 definitions), upgrade prices (100k-600k cash, 500-1500 RP), 21 regulation-change schedules with per-department flags, AI-vs-player mass handicap tweakables, driver salary contract stats, and a `hardcore` difficulty-settings row.
findings.confidence: proven (keys and ranges from the catalogue); values not dumped
findings.implications: Standard/Hard/Hardest presets are database ops gated by a `when` option; see HANDOFF §11.

findings.claim: A new career tile can be data-only: `career.mode` + `career.content` records in registry/career.json plus db rows (ModeChampionship, entrant list, content set), per the Decades recipe; Progressive's tile ships without a DLL for the tile itself.
findings.implications: Option B (separate My Team tiles per preset) is possible for data-group-scoped tables; global tables still apply profile-wide.

findings.claim: Verve's driver-row overrides and ai_driver_config keys apply to every AI-driven car in every mode (Driver Career, My Team, GP, TT): the per-car AI driver record is built at session setup from the driver row, with no career-specific path; only AI-controlled cars read it.
findings.implications: My Team gets Verve personalities for the AI field and the player's teammate.

findings.claim: In career modes each rating's `evolution` curve spans x = 0..10 seasons (start to peak) and freezes per season; v0.1 writes a flat pace curve and static overrides, which removes per-season driver development for the overridden characteristics.
evidence: docs/std/systems/drivers.md (Curve start/peak, 'Career season ratings are frozen when each season starts')
findings.implications: Issue 21: shift the stock curve instead of flattening it; per-season override rewrite needs a native hook.

findings.claim: An autonomous harness is feasible: `swofty run --apply --direct` launches and rolls back; a native plugin can fire menu routes, hand the player's car to the AI with sessions::set_control (as kizikafuka.ai-drive does), and exit on session.end; measurement via the game's official UDP telemetry (per-car lap/telemetry/status/damage and Overtake/Collision events, offline-capable) or the Swofty shared-memory feed; no headless mode exists, so tests run in real time on a GPU.
findings.confidence: inferred from docs; harness not built
findings.implications: HANDOFF §13; issue 24.

findings.claim: Stock driver_characteristics.* on driver rows are curated per driver and differ, often a lot, from the rating-curve output at season x=0 (row / curve): VER aggr 1.00/0.96, ctrl 0.96/0.74, mist 0.75/0.70, react 0.85/0.96, s_in 1.00/0.90, s_out 0.99/0.90; ALO 0.93/0.90, 0.97/0.69, 0.90/0.64, 1.00/0.90, 0.93/0.70, 0.94/0.70; BEA 0.65/0.84, 0.77/0.49, 0.65/0.41, 0.65/0.84, 0.68/0.49, 0.78/0.49. Which of the two the AI uses is UNKNOWN.
evidence: the curve table is named driver_characteristic_OVERRIDES; RE note: live record holds raw +0xf0 (from the row) and overrides +0x108 (negative = none)
findings.implications: Q-01 answered (stock is not -1). Precedence is Q-17 and the top open question: if the ratings win for drivers with a statistics holder, v0.1's row writes are no-ops for the whole 2025 grid and the generator must write rating curves instead (issue #7 decides; #6 depends on it).

findings.claim: The awareness_mistakes distribution is monotonic increasing (0:0, 0.5:0.2, 0.85:0.7, 1:1) and stock row values rank Alonso 0.90 > Verstappen 0.75 > Bearman 0.65, so 'mistakes' is mistake RESISTANCE (higher = fewer mistakes).
findings.implications: Q-03 static half: the generator default (proneness) is backwards; switch to --mistakes-is-skill semantics. Issue 8 confirms in a race batch.

findings.claim: 24 DriverStatisticsHolder rows carry a '2026' StatisticsDataSet (game_setup_modes f1_26, seasons season_2026): the 2025 grid plus arvid_lindblad. 71 holders have only 'default'; 22 F2 holders have 'default|f2_2026'.
findings.implications: Q-11 answered: the generator should write the pace rating to both 'default' and '2026' for those 24 drivers (issue 24).

findings.claim: ai_driver_config.* keys are not in the launcher's name catalogue: `db get <row>.ai_driver_config` and `db search` report nothing, but the full leaf path resolves by hash. 15 keys typed 'float' in docs/ai_driver_config_keys.* are curves (@v2@...).
findings.implications: v0.2 ops must address leaves by full path and write curve values for the 15 curve keys; tools/build_catalogue.py types need fixing.

findings.claim: Driver-row labels and statistics-holder labels differ for some drivers: holder alexander_albon vs row alex_albon; holders micheal_schumacher, aryton_senna, nilola_tsolov, john_benneet have no same-label row. The sample CSV's kimi_antonelli is not a row (the row is andrea-kimi_antonelli). 80 of 197 driver rows have no statistics holder.
findings.implications: The v0.1 smoke build would fail on Antonelli (row select). The generator must skip the rating write for drivers without a holder.
findings.correction: 2026-10-30 (#2 build): the holder labels above are their _metadata_ values, but DriverStatisticsHolder[driver=...] matches the holder's `driver` field, which equals the row label for all five (alexander_albon -> driver alex_albon, micheal_schumacher -> michael_schumacher, aryton_senna -> ayrton_senna, nilola_tsolov -> nikola_tsolov, john_benneet -> john_bennett). So no separate stats label is needed; only Antonelli's row label was wrong in the sample CSV. docs/stock/statistics_datasets.csv's 'driver' column is really _metadata_.

findings.claim: ai_driver_config.race_start reaction bounds are read per driver from the driver row: with all four bounds set to 0.65 on one driver per team, exactly that driver's car reacted at 0.650000 in both benchmark starts (9 of 10 teams), and the untagged teammate stayed stock.
findings.implications: Per driver in benchmark, for the 9 AI-controlled cars that took the tag (vehicle 19 ignores it, F-34). The per-driver ai_driver_config route works for race_start: v0.2a (#10) is partly unblocked (the race_start reaction bounds work). Part of Q-08 is answered: these keys are per driver. Equal bounds pin the reaction exactly, which makes them a precise instrument. It also gives a vehicle id -> driver map for benchmark Austria (docs/stock/vehicle_map_benchmark_austria.csv).

findings.claim: Benchmark vehicle 19 is Charles Leclerc's Ferrari and ignores ai_driver_config.race_start: tagged with 0.65 bounds it still started at 0.054 / 0.050 s, and it was the fastest starter in 5 of 7 stock starts. Most likely the player car (AI-driven in benchmark) on a different start path. Vehicle 8 is Lewis Hamilton.
findings.confidence: inferred (elimination from B-0005; the player-car part is a hypothesis)
evidence: B-0005 start 2: vehicle 19 reacted at exactly 0.050000, a round number, as if clamped or a fixed launch (supervisor review on #40)
findings.implications: Exclude vehicle 19 (and normally both Ferraris) from every arm and field statistic in benchmark batches. Optional later check (low priority): change the benchmark's player/driver key, if one exists, and see whether the 0.05 behaviour moves to another car.

findings.claim: B-0001: the driver-row reaction_speed effect is in the predicted direction but about half its predicted size (Alpine row 0.05 -> +0.042 s vs +0.075 predicted at k = 0.5), and the racecraft rating showed no effect (Racing Bulls 0.99 vs Sauber 0.05: -0.039 s, wrong way for 'ratings win'). Two open explanations for the half-size effect: (a) k is below 0.5 in these sessions; (b) the start uses something besides the row value.
findings.confidence: open (runtime, benchmark; inconclusive by the pre-set rule)
evidence: supervisor review on #38 (bootstrap: ROW gap z ~2.3, STATS gap z ~-1.1)
findings.implications: Q-17 leans 'row wins' in benchmark; B-0006 (#39, dose-response) is the follow-up.
findings.status: likely explained by F-36 (team-averaging noise; B-0006's per-driver slope matches k ~0.5)

findings.claim: In benchmark, the driver row's driver_characteristics.reaction_speed drives the AI race-start reaction and the racecraft rating does not: across four levels per source (per driver, 6 starts), the ROW slope is -0.109 s per unit (bootstrap SE 0.024, z -4.6) and the STATS slope is +0.068 (SE 0.029), positive, which is explained by the STATS drivers' untouched row values running against their levels (predicted +0.039 under row-wins).
evidence: runs/2026-10-30-B-0001/summary.md (#30): same direction, inconclusive by its own rule
findings.implications: Q-17 answered for benchmark: row wins. Writing driver rows (v0.1's mechanism) works for reaction_speed, at least in benchmark; #6 keeps the row-based plan. The slope gives k ~0.52 (mean = 0.35 - 0.21*k*r), consistent with B-0003. Grand Prix and career still need checking (harness gaps 2-3), and other characteristics may differ (B-0004 tests mistakes).
